parts.what: How the co-op staffs a response team at all hours on the kit's urgent safety line, what it can do, when it calls Police and how responders are supported, planned so other marketplaces can share it.

parts.name: Sexual harm reports
parts.what: A separate, trauma-informed path on the kit's sexual harm path: only trained responders see the report, the reporter is referred to specialist support and decides whether Police are told, and the trip record is kept.

features.name: After a crash
features.does: A driver involved in a crash reports it, gets help with insurance, and the rider is looked after.

parts.name: Ride crash report
parts.what: Records a crash with the trip, vehicle, people on board and photos on the kit's violence and crash handling, looks after the rider and sends the details to the driver's insurer.

features.name: Safe driving help
features.does: A driver sees speed limit alerts and gets gentle feedback on hard braking and phone use.

parts.name: Speed limit alerts
parts.what: Warns when over the posted limit, from open speed limit data matched to the driver's position.

parts.name: Driving feedback
parts.what: Private weekly feedback from phone sensors that only the driver sees.

features.name: Safety tips and education
features.does: Riders and drivers find short guides on staying safe.

parts.name: Safety guides
parts.what: Short safety guides in help, in English and te reo Māori first.

features.name: No driving impaired
features.does: Riders know no driver may drive under the influence of alcohol or drugs, and report a driver who seems impaired in one tap.

parts.name: Drug and alcohol rule
parts.what: A zero-tolerance rule that no one drives for Spare Ride under the influence of alcohol or drugs, in the published rules and the driver agreement.

parts.name: Impaired driver report
parts.what: A one-tap report during or just after a trip that the driver may be impaired, which points the rider to 111 if they are in danger and pauses offers to that driver until a person reviews it, under the safety pause rules.

features.name: Dashcam footage
features.does: A driver who runs their own dashcam tells riders, keeps footage only as long as the rules allow and shares it as evidence when something goes wrong.

parts.name: Dashcam rules
parts.what: Rules for drivers' own dashcams: notice to riders, what the Privacy Act asks and how long footage may be kept.

parts.name: Camera notice
parts.what: Tells riders on the driver card, before pickup, that the car records video or sound.

parts.name: Footage upload
parts.what: Lets a driver or rider upload footage as evidence for an incident or a dispute, added to the evidence bundle and deleted when the case closes.

areas.name: Accessibility
areas.summary: Rides for everyone: wheelchair accessible vehicles, assistance animals always carried, help to the car, apps that work with screen readers, deaf and hard of hearing drivers, booking by phone or by voice, Total Mobility and a simpler mode.

features.name: Wheelchair accessible rides
features.does: A wheelchair user books a vehicle with a ramp or hoist that is checked and fit for the job.

parts.name: Accessible vehicle check
parts.what: Records and checks ramps, hoists and restraints, with photos, before a vehicle offers accessible rides.

parts.name: Accessible ride option
parts.what: A ride option matched only to checked accessible vehicles, priced the same as standard.

parts.name: Accessible vehicle supply
parts.what: How many accessible vehicles each city needs and how the co-op helps drivers fund them.

parts.name: Wheelchair trip training
parts.what: Drivers who offer wheelchair trips complete ramp, hoist and wheelchair restraint training, tracked as a check with an expiry date before any wheelchair offer.

features.name: Assistance animals always carried
features.does: A rider with an assistance animal is never refused, and drivers know it.

parts.name: Assistance animal flag
parts.what: Riders note an assistance animal so the driver knows before arriving.

parts.name: Assistance animal rules
parts.what: The assistance animal part of the access duties: which animals must be carried and what a driver may ask, with sources.

parts.name: Refusal reports
parts.what: A fast report path for refused riders, with action under the published rules.

features.name: Help to the car
features.does: A rider who needs a hand asks for a driver trained to help them to and from the car.

parts.name: Assisted ride option
parts.what: A ride option for drivers who completed the assistance training.

parts.name: Assistance course
parts.what: A course on helping people with disabilities and older riders, made with disabled people's groups and run on the kit's training and certificates.

features.name: Works with screen readers and large text
features.does: A blind or low-vision person uses every screen with a screen reader, large text or high contrast.

parts.name: Accessible ride screens
parts.what: Live maps, the offer countdown and trip updates made usable with screen readers, large text and high contrast, on the kit's accessible components.

parts.name: Testing with disabled people
parts.what: Paid testing sessions with disabled riders and drivers before each release.

features.name: Deaf and hard of hearing drivers
features.does: A deaf driver gets flashing offer alerts and text-only contact, and riders are told to message instead of calling.

parts.name: Deaf driver mode
parts.what: Flash and vibration alerts, calls turned into a prompt to message, and a note to riders.

features.name: Book by phone call
features.does: A person without a smartphone books a ride by calling a phone line and gets updates by text.

parts.name: Phone booking line
parts.what: A phone number with a simple menu and a person to talk to, using a telephony provider at cost.

parts.name: Phone booking screen
parts.what: A screen for co-op staff to book, change and track rides for callers.

parts.name: Text and Relay booking
parts.what: People who cannot use a voice line book by text, or call through NZ Relay, and staff are trained to take Relay calls.

features.name: Total Mobility
features.does: A rider with a Total Mobility card gets their subsidised fare on Spare Ride.

parts.name: Total Mobility rules
parts.what: How councils approve operators, the subsidy, the card and reporting, region by region.

parts.name: Total Mobility card link
parts.what: Reads the rider's card, applies the subsidy and reports trips to the council.

parts.name: Total Mobility driver checks
parts.what: Tracks each driver's qualifications for each council's Total Mobility scheme, such as first aid and the NZQA unit standards Auckland Transport asks for, as checks with expiry dates.

features.name: Simple mode
features.does: An older or less confident rider uses a simpler app with bigger buttons and fewer steps.

parts.name: Simple mode
parts.what: A pared-back booking flow with saved places first and large text.

features.name: Accessibility needs on every request
features.does: A rider's access needs travel with every booking so the driver can prepare.

parts.name: Needs on request
parts.what: Sends the rider's chosen needs with the request and shows them on the offer.

features.name: Find the car without sight
features.does: A blind or low-vision rider gets sound and vibration cues as the car arrives and can ask the driver to come to them.

parts.name: Arrival cues
parts.what: Sound and vibration as the car nears and stops, and a standing request that the driver come to the door.

features.name: Room for a mobility aid
features.does: A rider with a folding wheelchair, walker or mobility scooter is matched with a car that has room for it.

parts.name: Mobility aid space
parts.what: Records boot space on vehicles and mobility aids on rider needs, and matches the two.

features.name: More time to get in
features.does: A rider who needs more time to board because of a disability sets it once in their needs, gets a longer free wait and never pays waiting charges.

parts.name: Extended wait setting
parts.what: A need set once on the rider's profile, on the rider's word, that lengthens the free wait and holds off waiting charges and the no-show clock.

parts.name: Waiting charge refund
parts.what: A rider with the longer wait set who is charged for waiting gets it back in one tap, with no review needed.

features.name: Read receipts with a screen reader
features.does: A blind or low-vision rider or driver reads their receipts, statements and logbook with a screen reader.

parts.name: Accessible ride documents
parts.what: Receipts, earnings statements, flat-rate credit notices and logbook exports made as tagged, accessible PDFs on the kit's accessible PDFs.

features.name: Easy read and NZ Sign Language
features.does: A person reads orientation, safety and key help pages in easy read or watches them in NZ Sign Language.

parts.name: Easy read and sign language versions
parts.what: Easy read and NZ Sign Language versions of driver orientation, safety guides and key help pages.

features.name: Drivers with an animal allergy
features.does: A driver with a documented allergy to animals is not sent assistance animal trips first, and the rider is not kept waiting or refused.

parts.name: Allergy re-offer rule
parts.what: Offers trips with an assistance animal to another driver first when a driver has a documented allergy, so the rider is not kept waiting or refused, with a lawyer checking the rule.

features.name: Book by voice
features.does: A blind or low-vision rider books, checks and cancels a ride by talking, to the app or to their phone's own voice assistant, without needing to see the screen.

parts.name: Voice booking
parts.what: Book, check and cancel a ride by speaking to the app: say where to, hear the fare and the driver's details read back, and confirm by voice. Asked for by a rider's friend who has lost her sight (r/cooperatives, 2026-10-19).

parts.name: Phone assistant shortcuts
parts.what: Book, check and cancel through the phone's own voice assistant (Siri on iPhone, Google Assistant on Android) using each platform's published shortcut and app action systems. How far this goes depends on the phone app approach.

areas.name: Ratings, reports, disputes and moderation
areas.summary: How trust is kept fairly: two-way ratings with published rules, reports, disputes decided by member panels while money is held, deactivation only with reasons and appeal, blocks, and moderation of profiles and messages.

features.name: Two-way ratings
features.does: A rider and a driver rate each other after each trip, and ratings follow published rules.

parts.name: Ride rating rules
parts.what: Which ride ratings are set aside, such as those caused by traffic, the app's route or the fare, and what ratings may be used for, voted by members on the kit's rating thresholds.

parts.name: Rating screen
parts.what: Stars and optional tags in one step, skippable.

features.name: Feedback tags and comments
features.does: A person adds tags such as "great conversation" or "unsafe driving" and a short comment.

parts.name: Feedback tags
parts.what: A short list of tags per side, each feeding a clear rule or simply thanks.

parts.name: Comment checks
parts.what: Flags abusive comments for a person to check before the other side sees them.

features.name: Report a problem
features.does: A rider or driver reports a problem with a trip or a person, and sees what happened next.

parts.name: Report flow
parts.what: Report categories, evidence and status updates, tied to the trip.

features.name: Disputes decided by members
features.does: When a rider and driver disagree about money or conduct, the money stays held and a panel of members decides.

parts.name: Dispute flow
parts.what: Opens a dispute, keeps the money held and collects both sides' statements.

parts.name: Evidence bundle
parts.what: Gathers the trip record, route, fare steps, chat, any shared recording and any uploaded footage for the panel.

parts.name: Balanced panels
parts.what: Panels for a rider's complaint against a driver include riders or independent members, and anyone with a conflict of interest steps aside.

parts.name: Settle before a panel
parts.what: Both sides can offer and accept a settlement before a panel sits, on the kit's settlement offers.

parts.name: Dispute deadlines
parts.what: Deadlines and reminders for each step of a ride dispute, on the kit's dispute clocks.

features.name: Deactivation only with reasons and appeal
features.does: A driver or rider is removed only under a published rule, is told which rule, and can appeal to a member panel.

parts.name: Deactivation rules
parts.what: The published list of what leads to a pause or removal, voted on by members.

parts.name: Appeal flow
parts.what: Lodge an appeal, see its status and get a reasoned decision.

parts.name: Safety pause rules
parts.what: A pause during an investigation has a set maximum length, the person is told it has started and why, a panel reviews it within set days, and a driver who is cleared gets back pay for the time lost under a voted rule.

features.name: Never matched again
features.does: A rider or driver chooses never to be matched with a particular person again.

parts.name: Block after a trip
parts.what: Offers never to be matched again on the rating and report screens, using the kit's blocking in dispatch.

features.name: Profiles and messages kept clean
features.does: Profile photos, names and messages that break the rules are caught and handled by people.

parts.name: Profile checks
parts.what: Checks names and photos against the rules, with a person deciding anything unclear.

parts.name: Chat reports
parts.what: Lets a person report a message, which sends the chat to a moderator.

features.name: Claim for damage or harm
features.does: A driver whose car was damaged by a rider, or who was hurt or threatened, makes a claim with evidence while any money stays held until a panel decides.

parts.name: Damage claim
parts.what: The driver claims for damage with photos and a repair quote, and the rider answers before a panel decides.

parts.name: Claim rules and limits
parts.what: What can be claimed, the evidence needed, how much can be held from the rider and the most charged without a panel, set by vote.

parts.name: Support after harm
parts.what: How a driver hurt or threatened by a rider is supported: Police, ACC, the co-op's insurance and any claim against the rider.

features.name: Take a dispute further
features.does: A rider or driver who is not satisfied learns how to take a dispute outside the co-op.

parts.name: Outside routes for rides
parts.what: Guidance on taking a ride dispute to the Disputes Tribunal or raising a concern with NZTA, on the kit's outside routes.

areas.name: Help, support and lost items
areas.summary: How people get help: a searchable help centre, help tied to a trip, lost items, fare reviews, driver support, the complaints register the law requires, and the staff tools behind it.

features.name: Help centre
features.does: A person searches plain help articles in their language.

parts.name: Ride help articles
parts.what: Short articles for riders and drivers, in English and te reo Māori first and then in languages such as Samoan and Tongan, kept as open text files in the kit's help centre.

parts.name: Help search
parts.what: Search over the articles, also usable offline in the app.

features.name: Help with a trip
features.does: A person picks a trip, says what went wrong, and gets an answer from a person or an automatic fix.

parts.name: Trip help screens
parts.what: Choose a trip, choose the problem, add details and see the reply.

parts.name: Something went wrong
parts.what: One entry on every trip that asks what happened and sends it to the right place: a safety incident, a sexual harm report, a report about a person, a fare review, a lost item or a dispute.

features.name: Lost items
features.does: A rider who left something behind contacts the driver through the app and arranges its return, with a return fee to the driver.

parts.name: Lost item flow
parts.what: Opens a masked contact with the driver for a set time after the trip and tracks the return.

parts.name: Return fee
parts.what: A published fee paid to the driver for returning an item.

parts.name: Unclaimed items
parts.what: How long a driver holds an item nobody collects, when it goes to Police, and how it is disposed of.

features.name: Fare review
features.does: A rider who thinks they were overcharged asks for a review and gets an automatic check first.

parts.name: Fare review
parts.what: Runs the route check and fare explainer, then refunds or sends to a person.

features.name: Driver support
features.does: A driver gets help with payouts, documents, offers and the app from people who know the work.

parts.name: Driver help hub
parts.what: A driver section of help with tickets for payouts, documents and safety.

features.name: Complaints register
features.does: Every complaint is recorded and kept for the time the law requires, ready for inspection.

parts.name: Complaints register
parts.what: Records complaints and their outcomes and keeps them for the required period.

parts.name: Register export
parts.what: Exports the register for an enforcement officer.

features.name: Support staff tools
features.does: A support worker sees the trip, the people and the history in one place and fixes things through the same commands as the app.

parts.name: Ride view in the support console
parts.what: Adds the trip, map, fare steps, messages and ride actions to the kit's support console, each action logged.

parts.name: Support roles
parts.what: What each support role may see and do, with least access by default.

features.name: Support staffing at cost
features.does: The co-op runs support with enough people at a published cost per trip.

parts.name: Support staffing plan
parts.what: Hours, staffing levels and cost per trip, published on the ledger.

features.name: Help from an AI assistant
features.does: A person asks an AI assistant that can look up their trips and act through the same commands, with a person always one tap away.

parts.name: Help assistant
parts.what: Lets the kit's help assistant look up Spare Ride trips and act through ride commands, with the person's own permissions and a person always one tap away.

areas.name: Businesses, families, taxis and fleets
areas.summary: Riding and driving as part of a group: family profiles, teen accounts, business accounts with invoices and policies, booking for guests, health and community transport, taxi companies joining, and fleet owners.

features.name: Family profile
features.does: A family shares one payment method, and the payer sees and can track family members' trips.

parts.name: Ride family group
parts.what: A payer and family riders sharing a payment method, with the payer able to see and track family trips, built on the kit's delegated access.

parts.name: Family screens
parts.what: Invite members, set the payer and see family trips.

parts.name: Tracking safeguards
parts.what: An adult in a family group is told their trips can be seen, sees who can see them, and can leave the group alone at any time; teen accounts are the only exception.

features.name: Teen accounts
features.does: A parent sets up an account for a teenager, with live tracking and extra safety checks on every trip.

parts.name: Teen riding rules
parts.what: Whether and how under-18s may ride alone in NZ, and what drivers must know.

parts.name: Teen account
parts.what: A linked account that always shares trips with the parent and always uses a PIN.

features.name: Business accounts
features.does: A business pays for staff rides on one monthly invoice, with spending rules and expense exports.

parts.name: Ride business settings
parts.what: Billing and ride settings for an organisation, on the kit's organisation accounts.

parts.name: Travel policy rules
parts.what: Limits by time, place, ride option and amount, checked at booking.

parts.name: Ride monthly invoice
parts.what: Ride's trip lines on the kit's business accounts on credit, which charges once a month with one tax invoice.

parts.name: Expense export
parts.what: Trip and invoice data in open formats that expense tools can import.

parts.name: Business dashboard
parts.what: Manage staff, policies, invoices and trips in a browser.

features.name: Book for guests
features.does: A hotel, venue or clinic books rides for guests who have no account, paid by the organisation.

parts.name: Guest booking screen
parts.what: Book and track rides for named guests from the business dashboard.

features.name: Health and community transport
features.does: A health provider or community group books and pays for rides for patients or members.

parts.name: Health information rules
parts.what: What the health information privacy rules require when rides are booked for patients.

parts.name: Partner billing
parts.what: Billing to a funder, with only the details they are allowed to see.

features.name: Taxi companies join
features.does: A taxi company brings its drivers and vehicles to Spare Ride while keeping its own brand on the car.

parts.name: Taxi company onboarding
parts.what: Adds a company with its own operator licence, its drivers and vehicles; rank and street-hail work stays under the company's own licence and camera rules.

parts.name: Taxi ride option
parts.what: A taxi ride option with an upfront fare or a meter, as the rules allow.

parts.name: Taxi dispatch links
parts.what: Which taxi dispatch systems have open, licensable interfaces to connect to.

features.name: Fleet owners
features.does: A person who owns several vehicles assigns them to drivers and sees what each earns.

parts.name: Fleet portal
parts.what: Vehicles, assigned drivers, documents and earnings in a browser.

parts.name: Fleet earnings split
parts.what: Splits earnings between fleet owner and driver on terms both can see.

parts.name: Fleet fairness rules
parts.what: Rules that protect drivers renting vehicles, set by member vote.

parts.name: Traffic notices to the driver
parts.what: Matches speed camera, red light and toll notices sent to a fleet vehicle's owner to whoever was driving it at the time, from trip and shift records, so the owner can name them.

areas.name: Co-op membership, voting and open costs
areas.summary: What makes Spare Ride a co-op: drivers join as members, vote on fares and rules, see the monthly cost ledger and where each trip's fee went, propose changes and elect panels.

features.name: Join as a member
features.does: A driver joins the co-op with one share and one vote, and a rider can join too if members agree.

parts.name: Ride member classes
parts.what: Driver members and, if members agree, rider members, as Spare Ride's classes on the kit's member register, kept within the kit's co-operative test so members who stop riding or driving do not tip the balance.

features.name: Vote on fares and rules
features.does: A driver votes on the fare formula, busy-time pricing, the fee and the rules, and the result changes the app.

parts.name: Vote screens
parts.what: Read a proposal, see its effect on example fares and vote.

parts.name: Vote results to settings
parts.what: Turns a passed Spare Ride vote into a settings change with a start date, using the kit's results to settings and only within the clearance held.

parts.name: Fare impact preview
parts.what: Shows what a proposed formula would do to typical trips and to driver earnings.

parts.name: Lessons from driver co-ops
parts.what: What worked and failed at existing driver co-ops, and why, so fares and votes are designed with their lessons.

features.name: Open cost ledger
features.does: Anyone sees what Spare Ride cost to run each month and what the fee paid for.

parts.name: Ledger page
parts.what: The monthly ledger for Spare Ride as a public page and open data.

parts.name: Ride cost lines
parts.what: The running costs that belong to rides, such as maps, routing, support and insurance.

features.name: Where my fee went
features.does: A rider or driver taps the fee on any trip and sees which costs it covered.

parts.name: Fee trace
parts.what: Links each trip's fee to that period's ledger lines.

features.name: Propose a change
features.does: A member writes a proposal, gathers support and puts it to a vote.

parts.name: Proposal form
parts.what: Write a proposal, see the support needed and track it.

features.name: Panels and the board
features.does: Members see how dispute panels are drawn at random from trained members, join the trained pool, and vote in board elections.

parts.name: Panel pool and board votes
parts.what: Members join the trained pool that the kit's panel selection draws from, and vote in the co-op-wide board elections on the kit's elections.

features.name: Surplus lowers the next fee
features.does: Any surplus at the end of a period lowers the next period's fee, shown on the ledger.

parts.name: Surplus rule
parts.what: Shows Spare Ride's surplus carried into the next fee, as worked out by the kit's fee setting.

features.name: Clear rules on who decides
features.does: A member sees who set the first rules, who may vote on each Spare Ride matter, and how an urgent change is made and then confirmed by members.

parts.name: Founding settings
parts.what: Who sets the first fare formula, fee and rules before any driver has voted, and the date by which members must confirm or change them.

parts.name: Ride electorate
parts.what: Who votes on what in Spare Ride: active drivers, fleet owners, taxi company drivers, each city's drivers on its own fares, and any votes riders join.

parts.name: Urgent changes in Ride
parts.what: Which Ride rules the co-op-wide urgent change power in the constitution may touch, such as safety rules and new legal duties, each published at once and put to members to confirm within a set time.

features.name: Riders have a say
features.does: A rider answers surveys on fares, safety and service and sees the results, without a vote.

parts.name: Rider surveys
parts.what: Non-binding surveys of riders on fares, safety and service, on the kit's consultations and surveys, with the results published.

areas.name: Operations and admin
areas.summary: The tools the co-op's own staff and elected members use to run the service: launching a city, watching it live, reviewing documents, catching fraud, handling incidents and official requests, logging every admin action and testing with simulations.

features.name: Launch a city
features.does: The co-op picks a city, sets its areas, ride options and fares, and switches it on when enough drivers are ready.

parts.name: First city decision
parts.what: Ranks NZ cities on riders, drivers, competition and rules.

parts.name: City settings
parts.what: Each city's areas, ride options, fares, fees and launch state as versioned settings.

parts.name: Launch checklist
parts.what: The steps to launch a city, from driver numbers and support hours to the outside security review and the privacy impact assessment, tracked in one place.

features.name: Watch the service live
features.does: The operations team sees live requests, trips, wait times and drivers online on a map.

parts.name: Operations map
parts.what: A live map with requests, drivers and trips, without showing riders' names.

parts.name: Live measures
parts.what: Wait times, unmatched requests, cancellations and drivers online, per area.

features.name: Review documents
features.does: A reviewer checks documents and photos the automatic checks could not, and approves or refuses with a reason.

parts.name: Document review queue
parts.what: A queue of checks for people, with the document, the rule and approve or refuse buttons.

features.name: Catch fraud
features.does: The co-op spots fake locations, duplicate accounts, stolen cards and trips faked to earn fares.

parts.name: Location fraud rules
parts.what: Ride's thresholds for impossible jumps and simulated locations in driver traces, on the kit's faked location checks.

parts.name: Duplicate account rules
parts.what: Ride's rules on the kit's fraud signals for one person running several accounts, or a banned person returning.

parts.name: Fake trip rules
parts.what: Ride's rules on the kit's fraud signals for riders and drivers who collude to create fares.

features.name: Handle incidents
features.does: The safety team sees open incidents, contacts people, pauses accounts and works with Police when needed.

parts.name: Incident console
parts.what: Open incidents by urgency with the trip, the people and the actions taken.

features.name: Official requests for data
features.does: The co-op answers Police and regulator requests only with proper legal authority, and publishes how many it gets.

parts.name: Ride records in official requests
parts.what: Which Ride records, such as trip records, traces and recordings, may be shared under the kit's law enforcement process, and what the passenger rules let officers see.

features.name: Every admin action logged
features.does: Every action a staff member takes is an operation in the log that elected members can audit.

parts.name: Ride staff roles
parts.what: What reviewers, the safety team and operations staff may see and do in Spare Ride, given and removed on the kit's admin console.

features.name: Uptime and monitoring
features.does: The co-op watches the service and publishes its uptime with the ledger.

parts.name: Ride health checks
parts.what: Checks and alerts for Spare Ride's own services, such as dispatch, quotes and live trips, on the kit's monitoring.

features.name: Test with simulated riders and drivers
features.does: The co-op runs a city full of simulated riders and drivers to test changes, train staff and give demos.

parts.name: Simulated riders and drivers
parts.what: Rider and driver behaviours for simulated city runs, using the same commands as people on real map data, ready to move into a shared kit simulator.

parts.name: Load tests
parts.what: Tests that a city's busiest hour runs smoothly before launch.

features.name: Supply and demand reports
features.does: Members see where and when riders went unserved and where drivers waited, to plan together.

parts.name: Supply and demand report
parts.what: Monthly report of unmet requests and idle time by area and hour.

features.name: Disaster mode
features.does: In a Civil Defence emergency, operations staff switch an area into disaster mode: busy-time pricing off, areas paused or limited, free trips where members agreed, and official alerts shown.

parts.name: Disaster mode switch
parts.what: One logged switch per area that turns off busy-time pricing, pauses or limits areas and allows free or subsidised trips under a rule members set in advance.

parts.name: Official alerts
parts.what: Brings in Civil Defence and other official alerts for the areas served and shows them to riders and drivers there.

parts.name: Drivers safe in emergencies
parts.what: Rules that drivers may go offline or refuse trips into danger with no effect on them, and a check-in for drivers in an affected area.

features.name: Tell drivers in an area
features.does: Operations staff send a notice to drivers online in a zone about a closure, an event or a safety warning.

parts.name: Area notices
parts.what: Sends a notice to drivers online in a chosen zone, read aloud if they are driving, with every notice logged.

features.name: Give a trip to a chosen driver
features.does: Staff offer a phone booking, Total Mobility trip or wheelchair trip to a named driver, who can still decline.

parts.name: Manual dispatch
parts.what: Offers a trip to a chosen driver with the reason logged; a decline carries no penalty and the trip goes back to normal dispatch.

features.name: Trips stay safe in an outage
features.does: When dispatch or payments are down for a city, trips under way finish, fares settle later, and riders and drivers are told plainly what is happening.

parts.name: Outage rules for trips
parts.what: Trips under way finish on the phones, fares settle from the stored quote when service returns, and new bookings pause.

parts.name: Outage notices
parts.what: Tells riders and drivers in a city what is down and what happens to their trip and pay, by push, text and the status page.

features.name: Service in quiet areas
features.does: People in rural towns and other quiet areas can book rides, even where few drivers work.

parts.name: Quiet area plan
parts.what: How to serve rural towns and other quiet areas, such as scheduled-only service, wider pickup ranges and taxi partners.

areas.name: Legal duties and compliance
areas.summary: What the law asks of a ride platform in NZ and how the app meets it: the operator licence, registered passengers instead of cameras, trip records, driver identification, agreed fares, drivers' status, health and safety, insurance, plain terms, consumer law and anti-money-laundering checks.

features.name: Hold the operator licence
features.does: The co-op holds the small passenger service licence that any ride app needs, with fit and proper people in control.

parts.name: Operator licence application
parts.what: What NZTA needs for the licence, who must pass the fit and proper check, and the NZ-resident representative.

parts.name: Licence duties list
parts.what: Every ongoing duty the licence brings, such as licence labels in vehicles, each linked to the part of the app that meets it.

features.name: Registered passengers instead of cameras
features.does: Every rider is a registered passenger, so vehicles need no in-car camera, and the records the rules ask for are kept.

parts.name: Registered passenger rule
parts.what: Makes sure no trip starts without identifying details for driver and rider, as the rule requires.

parts.name: Trip record retention
parts.what: Keeps the identifying details and trip records for the period the rules set, then deletes them unless another law needs them.

parts.name: Registered passengers on every booking path
parts.what: A ruling for each way a trip can be booked (for a guest, by phone, by a hotel or clinic, Total Mobility, taxi rank and street hail) on whether every passenger is a registered passenger, and what the vehicle needs if not.

parts.name: Booking path guard
parts.what: Stops any booking that would carry an unregistered passenger in a vehicle without an approved camera, and says why.

parts.name: No trips off the app
parts.what: A published rule that drivers and riders never use Spare Ride to set up trips outside it, since such a trip breaks the registered passenger rule and skips the GST the platform must collect.

features.name: Driver identification rules met
features.does: The co-op confirms whether the in-app driver ID meets the identification rule or a physical card is also needed.

parts.name: Driver identification rules
parts.what: Whether a digital ID in the app meets the rule, or a physical card is also needed.

features.name: Fare agreed before the trip
features.does: The upfront fare meets the rule that the fare or its basis is agreed before the trip starts.

parts.name: Fare agreement check
parts.what: Confirms the upfront quote, extras and fare changes meet the fare rules.

features.name: Drivers' status decided
features.does: The co-op decides whether drivers are employed worker-members or independent contractors, and the app follows that choice.

parts.name: Drivers' status decision
parts.what: Applies the kit's worker status test to Spare Ride's drivers after the Supreme Court ruling and the 2026 amendment, with a lawyer, and records the choice.

parts.name: Ride status settings
parts.what: Switches Ride's pay, work time, leave and agreement features on or off from the status set in the kit's worker status per app.

parts.name: Gateway test check
parts.what: If drivers are contractors, checks every driver-facing rule, such as required orientation, selfie checks, rating thresholds, area rules and deactivation, against the 2026 gateway test: a written agreement, freedom to work for others, no required availability or a right to subcontract, no ending for declining work, and a chance to get advice.

features.name: Health and safety duties
features.does: The co-op meets its health and safety duties to drivers and riders.

parts.name: Ride health and safety risks
parts.what: Ride's risks under the kit's health and safety duties, such as fatigue, violence from riders, crashes and phone use while driving, and how each is managed.

parts.name: Trip incidents in the register
parts.what: Crashes, assaults and serious injuries during trips go into the kit's incident register, each checked for whether it must be notified to WorkSafe, which for road crashes is unverified.

features.name: Insurance in place
features.does: Passengers, drivers and the co-op are insured as the law and good sense require.

parts.name: Ride insurance needs
parts.what: The cover rides add to the kit's co-op insurance, such as passenger liability and the platform's part in crashes, bought at cost.

features.name: Plain terms and policies
features.does: Riders and drivers get short, plain terms and a privacy policy that meet consumer law.

parts.name: Rider terms
parts.what: Rider terms in plain words, including the non-discrimination commitment and who sells each ride, checked against fair trading and consumer guarantees law.

parts.name: Privacy policy
parts.what: What is collected, why, for how long and who sees it, in plain words.

features.name: Anti-money-laundering check
features.does: The co-op meets the anti-money-laundering duties online marketplaces have had since 1 June 2025, covering the risks rides bring.

parts.name: Ride money-laundering risks
parts.what: The ride risks the kit's anti-money-laundering programme must cover, such as stored ride credit, cash and fake trips used to move money.

features.name: Duties to disabled riders
features.does: The service meets human rights law on access for disabled people and assistance animals.

parts.name: Access duties
parts.what: What human rights law requires of a ride service for disabled people, including refusals and charges such as waiting fees, with sources.

features.name: Rules tracked over time
features.does: The co-op notices when a law or rule changes and updates the app to match.

parts.name: Rules watch
parts.what: A list of the laws and rules Spare Ride depends on, each with an owner and a review date.

features.name: Fare vote cleared under competition law
features.does: Drivers vote on fares only in a way competition law allows, with any clearance from the Commerce Commission in place before the first vote.

parts.name: Ride fare vote and competition law
parts.what: Applies the kit's competition law check to drivers voting on a shared fare formula, which may be cartel conduct under the Commerce Act 1986 if they are contractors, and picks the route that makes it lawful.

parts.name: Commerce Commission clearance
parts.what: If needed, an authorisation under section 58, or a notice under any new collective bargaining regime for small businesses, before the first fare vote.

parts.name: Lawful vote limits
parts.what: Records which fare and fee questions members may vote on under the clearance held, so a vote outside it cannot be put.

areas.name: Privacy and data export
areas.summary: People own their data: download everything in open formats, delete what the law allows, keep data only as long as needed, protect locations, answer privacy requests, show drivers the data used about them and handle breaches.

features.name: Download my data
features.does: A rider or driver downloads all their data in open formats, including trips, routes, fares, ratings and messages.

parts.name: Ride export contents
parts.what: Adds trips, routes as GPX, fares, earnings, ratings and messages to the kit's data export, with a readme for each file.

parts.name: Export screen
parts.what: Ask for an export and download it when ready.

features.name: Delete my data
features.does: A person deletes their account and data, and is told what must be kept by law and until when.

parts.name: Ride deletion rules
parts.what: What deleting an account does to trips under way, held money, ride credit and open disputes, and which ride records the law keeps, on the kit's account deletion.

features.name: Keep data only as long as needed
features.does: The co-op keeps each kind of data only as long as the law or the service needs, then deletes it automatically.

parts.name: Retention schedule
parts.what: How long each kind of data is kept and why, from trip records to tax records.

features.name: Location privacy
features.does: A rider's exact addresses are hidden from the driver after the trip, and location history can be cleared.

parts.name: Address masking
parts.what: Shows drivers only the area of past pickups and drop-offs.

parts.name: Location history controls
parts.what: See and clear saved locations and recent places.

features.name: Privacy requests
features.does: A person asks to see or correct their personal information and gets an answer within the legal time.

parts.name: Privacy request tracker
parts.what: Logs access and correction requests about Ride data and tracks each legal deadline in working days with the kit's working day counter.

features.name: See the data used about me
features.does: A rider or driver sees every piece of data used in decisions about them, such as offers, ratings, fraud flags and pauses.

parts.name: Driver decision data view
parts.what: Shows a driver their offer history, ratings used, rule versions and any automated decision, with reasons.

parts.name: Rider decision data view
parts.what: Shows a rider the ratings used, any fraud flag or pause, the rule behind it and the data it rested on, except where the law allows it to be withheld.

parts.name: Ride decisions in the AI register
parts.what: Adds each automated decision in Ride, such as fraud flags, face matches, check-ins, automatic fare reviews and translation, to the kit's AI use register, with a way to ask a person to review it.

features.name: Breach response
features.does: If personal data leaks, the co-op tells the people affected and the Privacy Commissioner as the law requires.

parts.name: Ride breach risks
parts.what: Which Ride data would cause serious harm if leaked, such as live locations, home addresses and recordings, so the kit's breach response acts fast.

features.name: Open travel data
features.does: The co-op publishes anonymised travel time and demand data for cities and researchers.

parts.name: Anonymising methods
parts.what: Proven methods that stop people being found in published travel data.

parts.name: Open travel data
parts.what: Regular releases of travel times and demand by area and hour as open data.

parts.name: Māori data check
parts.what: Checks each release of travel data against Māori data sovereignty principles, with Māori advice, as well as against the anonymising methods.

features.name: Face checks within the biometrics code
features.does: A driver or rider asked for a face check is told why, what happens to their face data and what other way they have, as the Biometric Processing Privacy Code requires.

parts.name: Ride biometrics assessment
parts.what: Ride's proportionality assessment for each of its face checks (driver sign-up, the right-driver selfie, rider checks and photo checks), using the kit's biometric code compliance.

parts.name: Face check notices
parts.what: A plain notice before each face check, with another way to prove identity where the assessment calls for one.

parts.name: Limits on face data
parts.what: Keeps face results to the purpose assessed, never infers gender, mood or health from a face, and deletes face data on schedule.

features.name: Told when someone else gives us your details
features.does: A guest rider, trusted contact, staff member or patient whose details came from someone else is told who has them and why, as the Privacy Act has required since 1 May 2026.

parts.name: Indirect collection map
parts.what: Every Ride path that collects details from someone else, such as guest riders, trusted contacts, business staff, patients and phone bookings, with the notice each needs and any exception.

parts.name: Notice to the person
parts.what: Sends a short notice by text or email with a link to the privacy policy, unless an exception applies.

features.name: Driver locations kept private
features.does: Nobody can use the app, the API or published data to track a driver live or to find where they live.

parts.name: Driver position blurring
parts.what: Nearby cars shown to riders and the API are snapped to cells, delayed and capped in number, and hidden near where a shift starts or ends.

parts.name: Tracking and scraping limits
parts.what: Rate limits and pattern checks on arrival time and nearby car queries, so no one can follow a driver.

features.name: Privacy checked for the whole app
features.does: A rider or driver can read how the co-op checked the privacy risks of everything Spare Ride collects before launch.

parts.name: Ride privacy impact assessment
parts.what: A privacy impact assessment for all of Spare Ride on the kit's template, covering live location, trip traces, audio recordings, trusted contacts and demand maps.

areas.name: Languages, countries and poor signal
areas.summary: New Zealand first, international by design: many languages with te reo Māori first-class, local formats, country rule packs, payments and tax per country, local emergency numbers, local co-ops, data kept in region, and apps that cope with weak signal.

features.name: Many languages
features.does: A person uses the app in their language, starting with English and te reo Māori, with others added by volunteers.

parts.name: Te reo Māori review
parts.what: Paid review of Ride's te reo Māori text by fluent speakers before each release, through the kit's member translation.

features.name: Local formats
features.does: A person sees money, distances, dates and addresses in the way their country writes them.

parts.name: Ride units
parts.what: Distances in kilometres or miles and fare rounding for each country, on the kit's local formats.

features.name: Country rule packs
features.does: A new country's rules for licences, records, fares and work time are added as a pack without changing the core.

parts.name: Ride country pack
parts.what: The ride rules a country pack adds to the kit's country packs: licences, required records, fares and work time.

parts.name: Country research template
parts.what: The questions to answer about each new country's ride rules, with sources.

parts.name: Trip levies and local permits
parts.what: Per-trip government levies and booking service or operator permits by state or city, such as those in Australian states, as part of each country pack.

parts.name: Platform work laws overseas
parts.what: Laws on platform work in other countries, starting with the EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831, due in national law by 2 December 2026: a presumption of employment, open rules for automated management, human review and no processing of private conversations or off-shift data, and what Ride's audio recording and selfie checks would need there.

features.name: Payments and tax in each country
features.does: A rider pays in their own currency and the right tax is collected wherever the trip happens.

parts.name: Tax per country
parts.what: Ride's tax settings for each country on the kit's tax rules per country.

features.name: Local emergency numbers
features.does: The emergency button always calls the right number for the country the trip is in.

parts.name: Emergency numbers check
parts.what: Takes emergency numbers from the kit's country packs, starting with NZ's, and checks them before each city launch.

features.name: Local co-ops
features.does: Drivers in another country run their own co-op on the same software, joined to the federation.

parts.name: Ride for local co-ops
parts.what: What a country's ride co-op takes up when it joins, on the kit's name licence and federation register.

features.name: Data kept in region
features.does: A country's riders' and drivers' data stays in that country where the law asks.

parts.name: Ride data placement
parts.what: Which Spare Ride data must stay in each country, placed by the kit's data location service.

features.name: Works on weak signal
features.does: A rider or driver on a weak or patchy connection can still book, drive and finish trips.

parts.name: Low-data mode
parts.what: Fewer location updates, smaller trip messages and text fallbacks when the connection is poor, on the kit's light mode for slow connections.

parts.name: Weak signal tests
parts.what: Tests every key flow on slow and dropping connections and cheap phones.

areas.name: Apps, platform and open access
areas.summary: The apps and the open ways in: rider and driver apps on phones, a web booking page, background location, one command API for people, AI and scripts, an MCP server, plugins, booking links for other sites, the Spareware look and self-hosting.

features.name: Rider and driver apps on phones
features.does: A rider or driver installs Spare Ride on an Android phone or an iPhone.

parts.name: Rider app shell
parts.what: The rider app's navigation, screens and offline storage on top of the shared core.

parts.name: Driver app shell
parts.what: The driver app's navigation, screens and offline storage, built for use in a cradle.

parts.name: Ride app store listings
parts.what: Ride's own store needs, such as explaining background location and the ride-hailing rules, on top of the kit's app store rules.

features.name: Book in a browser
features.does: A rider books a ride from any browser without installing anything.

parts.name: Web booking page
parts.what: The booking flow as a fast web page that works on any device.

features.name: Location in the background
features.does: A driver's location keeps updating while the app is in the background, without draining the battery.

parts.name: Shift-long location
parts.what: The update rate, accuracy and battery settings a driver's shift needs, kept running in the background with the kit's location and background permissions.

parts.name: Battery tests
parts.what: Measures battery use over a full shift on common phones.

features.name: One command API
features.does: Everything a person can do in Spare Ride, a script or AI agent can do through the same commands.

parts.name: Ride command set
parts.what: Every ride action as a typed command on the kit's operation layer, with permissions.

parts.name: Query API
parts.what: Read access to trips, fares, earnings and settings with the caller's own permissions, with driver positions only ever blurred.

parts.name: API documentation
parts.what: Open documentation of every command and query with examples.

parts.name: Ride events for webhooks
parts.what: A published list of ride events sent through the kit's webhooks: booked, driver assigned, arrived, started, completed, cancelled and receipt ready.

features.name: AI agents
features.does: A person lets an AI agent book rides or check earnings for them, with approval before it spends, and staff use agents for routine work, all through the same commands.

parts.name: Ride agent rules
parts.what: Which ride commands need the person's approval, such as booking, tipping or cancelling with a fee, and default spending limits, using the kit's approval steps and agent limits.

parts.name: No automated offer taking
parts.what: A published rule that only the driver, in the driver app, can accept offers; scripts and agents may read offers and earnings but never take trips, to keep shares fair and drivers within the phone rule.

parts.name: Agent labels and limits
parts.what: Labels bookings and messages an agent makes, keeps ratings, dispute statements and votes for people only, and treats pickup notes and chat as data an agent never obeys.

features.name: Plugins
features.does: Members add checked plugins, such as a city's dispatch rules or a new report.

parts.name: Plugin points
parts.what: The places in Spare Ride where a sandboxed plugin can add rules, screens or reports.

features.name: Booking links for other sites
features.does: A venue, event or website adds a Spare Ride booking button or link with the destination filled in.

parts.name: Booking links
parts.what: Links that open a booking with pickup and destination filled in.

parts.name: Booking widget
parts.what: A small booking box other sites can embed.

features.name: The Spareware look
features.does: Spare Ride looks and works like every Spareware app, with its own light colour.

parts.name: Spare Ride design tokens
parts.what: Colours, type and parts from the Spareware design guide, with Spare Ride's own colour.

features.name: Run your own server
features.does: A member group runs its own Spare Ride server and connects it to the co-op.

parts.name: Ride in the self-host package
parts.what: Adds Spare Ride's services to the kit's self-host package, with a guide for running a city.

assess: Is there anything you do in Uber or a taxi app today, as a rider or a driver, that has no feature in this map?
Could the first city launch with only the core features, or is something marked next that riders would miss on day one?
Is the fare card clear in five seconds: the fare, the driver's share, the at-cost fee, the payment fee and GST?
Would a driver trust the offer card: does it show everything needed to decide, and is declining clearly free?
Can the dispatch rules be published in one page and still work fairly at airports, events and quiet times?
Is the drivers' status decision (RD01) far enough along to build pay, work time and the driver agreement, or should those parts wait?
Can the co-op get access to the official licence and vehicle registers, or does sign-up start with people reviewing documents?
Should Spare Ride build its own approved electronic logbook, or have drivers use an existing approved one at first?
Are the core safety tools at least as good as the incumbent's on day one: emergency button, trip sharing, PIN, check-ins and a response team?
Does the first city have enough wheelchair accessible vehicles, and should phone booking and Total Mobility be in the first release?
Once support staff, the safety team, insurance, telephony and maps are on the ledger, what does the at-cost fee per trip come to?
Which kit services (payments, matching, maps, trust) must exist before Spare Ride can start, and who is building them?
Are the part sizes believable, and which large parts (routing, address search, navigation, background location, payments, GST engine, the apps) carry the most risk?
Does every screen in the demo come from what people need to do, with nothing copied from an incumbent's interface?
Does anything here need a lawyer before it is built: cameras and registered passengers, recording audio, women preferences, teen accounts, cash, stored credit?
Can drivers lawfully vote on a shared fare under the Commerce Act, and does the co-op need a Commerce Commission authorisation before the first vote (RIDE-A20-F12)?
Do the face checks at sign-up and during shifts pass the Biometric Processing Privacy Code's proportionality test, and what other way is there for people who will not use their face (RIDE-A21-F9)?
Who sells each ride, the co-op or the driver, and do the receipt, the tax invoices and the rider terms all match that choice?

If drivers are contractors, does every driver-facing rule pass the 2026 gateway test check, and if RD01 decides they are employees, are pay records, leave and rosters (RIDE-A10-F6) moved to core before launch?
Has the kit raised the parts Spare Ride's core depends on, such as adding a vehicle, turn-by-turn directions, light mode and trip check-ins, or does launch wait for them?
Do the safety tools cover the worst harms from day one: the separate sexual harm path, impaired driver reports, and limits on safety pauses?
Do disabled riders get the longer free wait with no waiting charges, and do receipts show the driver's identification and the vehicle's registration?
